classification.difficultyReason: Derive a quadratic area rule from a fixed perimeter, restrict its domain using positive side lengths, and sketch the restricted parabola.

content.prompt: Jordan is playing with a $20\text{ cm}$ piece of copper wire, which he bends into the shape of a rectangle, as shown. Let $x$ be the length of a side of the rectangle.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle wider than it is tall, with x beside the right vertical side; no other measurements.
spec.mathematics: A rectangle with one side labelled x.
spec.answerVisibility: Given figure visible in all editions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area $A$ of the rectangle as a function of $x$.

answer.worked:
Let the other side length be $w$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}2x+2w&=20\\x+w&=10\\w&=10-x\end{align*}$$
Hence $A(x)=x(10-x)\text{ cm}^2$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the fact that lengths must be positive to find the domain of $A$.

answer.worked: Both side lengths must be positive: $x>0$ and $10-x>0$. Thus $x>0$ and $x<10$, so the domain is $(0,10)$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Sketch the graph of $A$ for the domain you found in part b.

answer.short: A downward-opening parabola with vertex $(5,25)$ and open endpoints at $(0,0)$ and $(10,0)$.
answer.worked: $A(x)=x(10-x)$ is a downward-opening parabola with zeroes at $x=0$ and $x=10$. Its axis of symmetry is $x=5$, and $A(5)=5(10-5)=25$. Sketch only $0<x<10$, using open circles at the excluded endpoints.

spec.description: Restricted downward parabola with open endpoints, x ticks at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and area ticks at 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. No grid.
